name: Chicago School terracotta
summary: Thin, fireproof terracotta cladding on the steel frames of early skyscrapers. Architects in Chicago used it for flat, white or cream walls and for flowing plant ornament.

philosophy.core_thesis: When a steel frame carries the load, the wall becomes a skin: a thin clay tile protects the steel from fire and carries the ornament.
design_principles: Hang a thin hollow terracotta tile on the steel frame; the tile carries no load.
Keep the wall flat and divided in a grid that shows the frame behind it.
Use a cream, buff or white glaze, so that the clay shows the same colour from the street.
Model the ornament as flowing plants and geometric knots, in low relief, over the piers and the spandrels.
Fire the tile hard so that it protects the steel from fire and rain.
Make each piece in a mould, and fit it to a number on the plan.
Cover the whole facade with one material, from the base to the cornice.
anti_patterns: Heavy classical ornament with no link to the frame
A dark brick wall with no cladding
Glossy, bright colour on the whole facade

form.shape: Hollow cladding blocks for piers and spandrels, window surrounds, cornices, capitals and large relief panels.
form.profile: A flat face with a low, crisp relief; the ornament rises 1 to 3 cm and flows over the whole panel.
form.foot_and_rim: Each tile has square edges with a small lip for the joint and an open back with webs, which hold the anchor.
form.proportion: A tile is about 30 to 60 cm wide and 5 to 10 cm thick; a spandrel panel can be 1 m wide.
rules: Make the tile hollow and thin.
Show the grid of the frame on the wall.
Use low relief that flows across tiles.
Keep the colour in one pale family.

bodies.rule: Use a fine, even terracotta that fires pale, so that a thin glaze or a clear slip gives a cream or white surface. The tile must be hard and without large pores.

methods: drying in a heated drying room
forming.joins: Tiles are hung on steel anchors and rods on the frame, with thin joints of cement mortar between them.
forming.details: A mould seam on the back, an anchor slot, a number or mark on the edge, and a thin, bright glaze line at the joint.

glaze.pattern: Plant and geometric ornament in low relief on piers, spandrels and cornices; the wide fields between are plain, in cream or white.
glaze.gloss: Satin to matt, about 10 to 50 GU; some tall buildings used a bright white glaze of about 70 GU.
glaze.wear: The tile weathers well; the glaze crazes with age, and a few tiles lose a corner at the edge.

palette.strategy: A pale, clean colour on the whole wall: white, cream or light buff, with a little green or red in the ornament of the base.

firing.kiln: A large downdraught kiln, often in Chicago or on the east coast, with saggars for glazed work.
firing.scale: Several large companies made the tile; a single tower used tens of thousands of blocks.
firing.signs: A numbered back, a thin mould seam and a small mark of the maker on the edge.

pieces.form: Spandrel tile in cream glaze with a low plant knot
Panel of flowing leaf ornament for a pier base, in bare clay
Flat glazed white tile that covers a whole bay of the frame
Pier head with a geometric knot and a ring of leaves

positive: cream glazed terracotta tiles on a steel frame
flowing plant ornament in low relief
flat grid facade with bay windows
spandrel panels with a knot motif
white terracotta tower in clear light

evidence.title: Guaranty Building, Buffalo, New York, October 2012 - 01.jpg

emotion.target_response: Modern confidence: the viewer sees a tall, light wall that shows its frame and carries a fine plant ornament.

use_cases: a render of an early skyscraper with terracotta skin
a conservation note on a terracotta tile facade
a spandrel panel design in low relief
avoid_when: the brief needs a heavy stone wall
the brief needs a curtain wall of glass
the brief needs a deep, dark Victorian relief

modifiers.how: Make the blocks thicker, add two clay colours and deepen the relief to 5 cm or more.
Change to a bright blue-green or gold glaze and use zigzag and stepped ornament.

ornament_level.note: The tile skin is thin and flat; the ornament does not carry load.

wall_thickness.note: A thin cladding tile has a wall of 5 to 12 mm in its ribs and 25 mm at the face.
